analysis.title: 10 Charts We're Talking About (22 Oct 2026)
key_insights: AI complex has had a rough couple of weeks. Tesla cut capex, Meta's AI spending raised cost concerns, and Lam Research guidance underwhelmed, which reignited doubts about the durability of the AI trend.

Before the weakness, hedge funds were heavily short and sold tech at a record pace. GS prime data as of 19Oct showed the largest two-week net selling of Global Info Tech in its 10y+ record (-3.3 std dev), with short leverage at the 99th percentile on a 5-year view.
Credits of lower-rated borrowers have been the center of stress as the market reassesses AI buildout economics under potentially higher-for-longer long-term rates and possible energy cost pressures.

GS strategists remain underweight USD IG Tech and neutral USD HY. They expect dispersion across AI-related issuers to stay high, particularly in project finance bonds, where data centers (including chip/compute financing) have dominated issuance.

Brent hit fresh local highs after headlines on possible US/Israel strikes on Iran after elections, a US order for diplomats to leave Saudi Arabia amid Houthi strikes, and Saudi Aramco telling staff to evacuate its Dhahran headquarters. Attacks in the Strait of Hormuz have become more frequent over October.

USD rates remain better bid despite Middle East risk. The desk suspects the market sees the NYT report as unconfirmed and deniable by the Trump Administration, while the AI de-rating looks more sustained (neocloud/hyperscaler credit stress, semis weakness). Real yields are driving.

French bond stress is intensifying as lawmakers grapple with the debt burden while protestors riot over cost of living. 10y OAT/Bund spreads are the widest since the euro was introduced, and the absolute yield is higher than in the Eurozone crisis.

GS strategists see energy price relief as the clearest route to OAT/Bund spread compression: it improves the growth and deficit risk skew, gives core rate relief with limited ECB tightening, and lower rates volatility encourages carry strategies. Without it, they expect wider spreads and more pressure on EUR FX.
There has been demand for EURUSD downside in recent weeks. EUR vol is still low on a long-term lookback, and the EUR discount to USD real yield differentials gives some valuation cushion for hedges.
Overlay hedge interest has also appeared in USDJPY puts. JPY screens about 40% undervalued vs USD on long-term fair value models, partly reflecting Japanese savings redeployed into US assets.
If AI concerns spiral into US-unexceptionalism and US-Japan rate differentials compress, GS expects sustained repatriation from the US into Japan (USD selling, JPY buying).

The USDJPY put hedge is supported by Japanese officials' interest in a strong JPY, PM Takaichi's call for more domestic investment in local financial assets, and signs the BoJ will keep hiking gradually. Japan's biggest labour group is seeking a 6% midpoint target for 2027 wage talks.

Equities-down / yields-down dual binaries continue to trade as growth shock hedges, and the desk likes this implementation. Realized correlations have flipped back to AI down, 10y yields lower and USD softer vs JPY.
